prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: a fence blown down. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a fence has been blown down, I first check whether the damage is isolated to the boundary or part of broader storm harm to sheds, gates or roofing, because that usually tells me whether the claim stays straightforward within delegated authority."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the policyholder says the fence fell in high winds, I look for a weather link rather than the word ‘storm’ alone, since a gusty day is not the same as a properly evidenced weather event."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the photos show loose panels, rotten posts or long-term leaning before the weather, I prefer to treat that as wear and tear unless there is clear evidence the wind was the main cause of the collapse."},{"type":"observation","content":"When only one or two bays are down and the rest of the boundary is intact, I usually treat the loss as partial and keep the repair scope tight to the damaged section only."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the fence is a shared boundary, I check who owns which section and whether there may be a contribution from a neighbour, because that can change both liability and what we can settle."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a claim includes makeshift repairs, I prefer to accept reasonable temporary securing costs if they are modest and clearly aimed at preventing further damage or keeping pets and children safe."},{"type":"observation","content":"When there is damage to posts or fixings but the panels are reusable, I look for a repair option before replacement, because like-for-like repair is often enough for delegated handling."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the fence is part of a wider storm claim, I compare the timing and pattern of damage with the reported weather to make sure the fence loss fits the same event rather than being a separate maintenance issue."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the policyholder has no photos from before the incident, I prefer to use the post-loss images and any repairer notes to infer condition, rather than refusing solely because the pre-loss state is not documented."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the boundary runs onto a public footpath or road, I pay extra attention to safety and debris removal, because the immediate risk may matter as much as the repair cost in the triage decision."}]}
